messages:
maria (Support): heads up — multiple customers started seeing 401s right after the scheduled key rotation at ~02:14 UTC. tickets: #5421, #5428, #5432. customers report 'invalid_token' in responses. @sara can you take oncall?

sara (Oncall): on it. I'm paging logs now. I'm seeing a spike of token validation failures immediately after the rotation job finished. Putting the affected service into maintenance mode for now.

maria (Support): attaching a sample curl from a customer: 
```
curl -i https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJI..."
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "description": "kid not found in jwks"
}
```

devraj (eng-runtime): looking at the rotation job logs. rotation job appears to have run and committed new keys to the key-store, but the cache invalidation step failed with a timeout to redis. copying relevant bits: 
```
2026-03-14T02:14:12Z INFO rotate-keys: generated new keyset id=ks_20260314_0214
2026-03-14T02:14:12Z INFO rotate-keys: published jwks to /keystore/ks_20260314_0214
2026-03-14T02:14:13Z ERROR rotate-keys: failed to flush jwks cache err="dial tcp 10.0.5.23:6379: i/o timeout"
2026-03-14T02:14:13Z WARN rotate-keys: rotation partially applied, published keys but cache flush failed
```

jin (SRE): that lines up with metrics — redis replication lag at that window jumped and timed out connections from the batch-job pod. If the new jwks wasn't in the cache for the auth instances, tokens signed with the new kid would fail. Two mitigation paths: 1) force a manual cache flush + restart auth pods, or 2) rollback the rotation to previous keyset while we fix the pipeline.

sara (Oncall): can we try manual flush first — less customer-visible change. devraj, can you run the flush and restart once done? I'll coordinate with support to call out mitigations to customers.

devraj (eng-runtime): running manual commands now:
```
# flush cache for jwks namespace
redis-cli -h redis-primary DEL auth:jwks:cache
# rollout bounce auth deployments
kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-service -n prod-auth
```

deploy-bot: Rollout restart started for deploy/auth-service (3 pods) by devraj at 2026-03-14T02:29:05Z

sara (Oncall): auth pods are restarting; watching logs.

~5m later~

maria (Support): customers in tickets #5421 and #5432 confirm they're seeing 200s again for the same requests. still waiting on #5428 confirmation.

jin (SRE): monitoring shows 401s dropping back to baseline. redis errors cleared after the manual flush. The rotation job should have marked itself partial — we need to decide whether to re-run rotation (with improved retry) or rollback.

devraj (eng-runtime): the rotation job's state is 'committed' in the keystore but the auth instances didn't load new keyset until after the manual flush. There is a small window where some requests went to instances that hadn't refreshed their jwks cache. I'm recommending we roll back the rotation to be safe and re-run with stricter cache guarantees.

luis (Product): impact assessment — ~6 customers made support tickets, a handful of 5xx/401 alerts for internal dashboards, customer-visible error window ~14 minutes (02:14–02:28 UTC). This looks P1 for customer impact.

sara (Oncall): rolling back now to previous keyset to normalize state across fleet. devraj, initiating rollback job.

deploy-bot: Key rotation rollback initiated by devraj at 2026-03-14T02:36:40Z
deploy-bot: Rollback completed at 2026-03-14T02:40:12Z — keyset restored to ks_20260307_1801

maria (Support): Confirmed with remaining customer (#5428) — requests are normal. Closing the high-priority customer escalations after notifying them of mitigation. :thumbsup:

sara (Oncall): declaring incident mitigated at 02:45 UTC. Setting severity: high -> mitigated. We'll keep monitoring for 24 hours.

luis (Product): action items for postmortem: 
- fix rotation pipeline to treat cache flush failures as fatal (atomic rotate) or add retries/backoff
- add pre-rotation canary that verifies at least one auth instance loaded jwks
- add integration test that simulates redis lag during rotation
- improve observability: rotation job should emit explicit 'cache_flushed' metric and alert on failures
- add a runbook for manual recovery (redis flush + pod bounce) and expose the commands to SRE/support runbooks

devraj (eng-runtime): I'll open PR today to change rotate-keys behavior: make cache flush a blocking retry with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts, and fail rotation if flush never succeeds. Also adding post-rotation verification (curl auth/.well-known/jwks) from k8s job.

jin (SRE): I'll add a monitor on rotate-keys job errors and a paging alert when cache flush fails. Also will add redis replication lag guard rails for critical jobs.

maria (Support): I've drafted customer-facing post-incident message and will run it by legal for copy.

sara (Oncall): scheduling postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 PT. tagging owners: @devraj, @jin, @luis. Thanks all — nice quick coordination.

ticket-bot: Tickets updated: #5421 CLOSED, #5432 CLOSED, #5428 CLOSED — root cause: partial key rotation due to cache flush timeout (redis replication lag).

---
Notes: timeline and logs collected, follow-up PRs linked in the postmortem doc.
